What is GATE Exam?

The GATE is also called as Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering , which is a national-level entrance test held once a year to offer to offer admission to MTech and research programmes in IITs, IIITs, NITs, IISc, and other GFTIs. Every year, the exam is conducted by IISc, followed by IITs on a rotational basis.
This year, IIT Guwahati is conducting GATE exam .

GATE 2026 Syllabus

IIT Guwahati released the GATE 2026 syllabus along with the information brochure. The GATE previous year's question paper consists of three major sections - General Aptitude, Engineering Mathematics and the core subject that the candidate has opted for. The general aptitude syllabus is common for all subjects.

The GATE Question paper will have 65 questions for 100 marks, including 15 marks for general aptitude questions. The paper codes AR, CY, EY, GG, MA, PH, XH, and XL will have 15 marks for general aptitude & the remaining 85 marks are devoted to the specific subject. A ll other paper codes except AR, CY, EY, GG, MA, PH, XH and XL will have 15 marks for general aptitude , 13 marks for engineering mathematics and the remaining 72 marks for the specific subject.

Candidates must choose the paper combination from the subject list curated by the conducting authorities. For a paper conducted in multiple sessions, a candidate will be mapped to appear for the exam in one of the sessions only.

blocks.value: GATE COAP 2026 Counselling Process

The COAP - Common Offer Acceptance Portal is a common portal for all participating institutes to fill all IIT MTech seats for GATE-qualified candidates. The GATE COAP is conducted in five main and five additional rounds. Candidates will be given three options - accept and freeze, retain and wait, and reject and wait. On the other hand, in the additional rounds, candidates have only two options to consider - accept and freeze, and reject. Let's look at it details -

value: If a candidate selects - accept and freeze, then it means that he/she is willing to accept the offer and do not want to upgrade to higher preferences
If a candidate selects- retain and wait, then it means he/she is willing to accept one of the available offer, however, he/she want to be considered for upgrading to higher preferences.
Lastly, if a candidate select - reject and wait, then it means he/she is not willing to accept the offer and want to be considered for upgrading for higher preferences

blocks.value: GATE CCMT 2026: Counselling Process

Centralised Counselling for M.Tech./M.Arch./M.Plan (CCMT) is a common platform for GATE-qualified candidates to take admission to NITs, IIITs & other GFTIs. GATE CCMT  counselling process consists of three regular rounds, two special rounds (SR) & a national spot round (NSR). Candidates will be given four choices for the allotted seats: Float , Slide, Freeze & Surrender (Participate in the next round).

value: Float: Retaining choices of previous rounds & willing to opt for better choices in further rounds.
Slide : Retaining choices of previous rounds of the same institute & willing to opt for better choices in further rounds.
Freeze: No change in Seat Allotment; however, willing to opt for category upgradation.
Surrender (Participate in the next round): No claim on the surrendered seat in further rounds & willing to opt for the better opportunity.

40 marks in GATE will approximately give a rank between 2000 to 5000 depending on the paper difficulty level and the number of registered candidates in that particular branch. Obtaining 40 marks is mainly considered average, opening chances to a few new IITs (less popular branches) and NITs.

However, rank for 40 marks in the Graduate Aptitude in Engineering can give a different rank value for different branches and disciplines. For example, 40 marks in GATE CSE can correspond to 2000 to 5000 rank. On the other hand,  40 marks in GATE ME, can correspond to 2700 - 7100 rank.
Advice to students who secured 40 marks in GATE exam : Better to apply in some state-level colleges or new NITs.

blocks.value: Attempting all questions of GA in GATE can easily fetch you 15 marks. So, to prepare for general aptitude, start with knowing the syallabus. Start with topics that you find easy. Practice and keep a target of solving at least 30 to 50 questions a day- 20 questions (easy level),  20 questions (mid-level), and 10 questions (hard level). Increase this frequency slowly.

blocks.value: Important FAQs Regarding GATE 2026 Syllabus
Check Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) related to the GATE 2026 syllabus.
The GATE CS is one of the most demanding paper taken by the aspirants. Here are some of the important high-weightage topics and chapters that are frequently asked in the GATE exam every year.
Every year, more than 8 to 12 marks of questions are extracted from these topics. The questions range from easy to challenging. So, it is advisable to focus on these topics for GATE preparation.
Candidates can check GATE exam pattern and question distribution of the papers - AR, CY, DA, EY, GG, GE, MA, PH, ST, XH, and XL below -

value: General aptitude section carry 15 marks and subject mark consists questions of 85 marks
Total marks of GATE question paper - 100 marks

blocks.value: Honestly, textbooks are not enough for GATE preparation (especially if you are targeting IITs and top colleges).

Besides your college books, look out for top GATE books recommended by toppers, mentors, and professors. Pick at least one standard book for each subject and start studying it side by side. Apart from that, also practice solving GATE question papers of last 5 to 10 years to get hands on the question difficulty and pattern.
Stay consistent, prepare a practical timetable and religiously follow it. At the end, it's all upto how you prepare for the exam.

There is no ideal time to start the GATE preparation. Start early (from the first year itself). It is mainly because your bachelor's topics and chapters have the most weightage in the GATE question paper. The topics that are taught in your third year are the backbone. If you are clear with the fundamentals and concepts (taught in classes), then you do not require extra time to prepare for GATE. Just revise and practice questions. That's enough.
So, start preparing for GATE right from the first year. Your brain is fresh with the concepts and formulas, thus making it easy to solve the questions and prepare for the exam.

faqs.question: Is there any change in the GATE 2026 syllabus?
faqs.answer: No, there is no change in GATE 2026 syllabus. However, a new sectional paper has been added under Engineering Sciences, XE, which is Energy Science and GATE paper code is XE-I. Candidates can download GATE syllabus 2026 PDF from official website- gate2026.iitg.ac.in.

faqs.question: Where can I download the latest GATE syllabus for preparation?
faqs.answer: Candidates can download GATE syllabus from the official website - gate2026.iitg.ac.in. The syllabus is available in PDF format. Before downloading, check the GATE paper code and branch name. The GATE exam syllabus is available for 30 papers.

faqs.question: For how many subjects is the GATE exam conducted?
faqs.answer: The GATE exam is conducted for 30 subject papers. In 2024, the GATE Data Science and Artificial Intelligence was introduced. Each subject or branch is determined by a paper code which applicant must note carefully. While filling out the application form, candidates must check the GATE branch and paper codes and add them.

faqs.question: Can I download the GATE question papers for free?
faqs.answer: Yes, candidates can download GATE question papers for free. The GATE exam papers are available in PDF format and can be downloaded for free. IIT Guwahati has activated GATE mock test 2026 link for students to practice.

faqs.question: Is the General Aptitude Syllabus common for all branch papers in GATE?
faqs.answer: Yes, the GATE General Aptitude syllabus is common for all branch papers in GATE. Candidates must check the GATE syllabus PDF carefully before starting their preparation. The GATE GA syllabus includes the following - Verbal aptitude (basic English grammar and vocabulary) Quantitative Aptitude - Data interpretation and numerical computation and estimation Analytical Aptitude and Spatial Aptitude

faqs.question: How to prepare for General Aptitude in GATE 2026?
faqs.answer: Attempting all questions of GA in GATE can easily fetch you 15 marks. So, to prepare for general aptitude, start with knowing the syallabus. Start with topics that you find easy. Practice and keep a target of solving at least 30 to 50 questions a day- 20 questions (easy level),  20 questions (mid-level), and 10 questions (hard level). Increase this frequency slowly. Besides that, practice GATE old question papers to understand, what kind of questions are asked (under GA). Follow the same pattern and find similar questions to solve. If you keep up this frequency, then sure shot you will score full marks in GATE general aptitude.

faqs.question: How many reasoning and comprehension questions asked in GATE 2026 question paper?

faqs.question: What are the most important GATE Civil Engineering topics to score 60+ marks in GATE?

faqs.question: What are some important topics in GATE Computer Science and Engineering?
faqs.answer: The GATE CS is one of the most demanding paper taken by the aspirants. Here are some of the important high-weightage topics and chapters that are frequently asked in the GATE exam every year. Data Structures and Algorithms Theory of Computation Operation Systems Databases and Computer Networks. Every year, more than 8 to 12 marks of questions are extracted from these topics. faqs.question: Is it enough to rely on the college text books for GATE 2026 preparation?
faqs.answer: Honestly, textbooks are not enough for GATE preparation (especially if you are targeting IITs and top colleges). Besides your college books, look out for top GATE books recommended by toppers, mentors, and professors. Pick at least one standard book for each subject and start studying it side by side. Apart from that, also practice solving GATE question papers of last 5 to 10 years to get hands on the question difficulty and pattern. Stay consistent, prepare a practical timetable and religiously follow it. At the end, it's all upto how you prepare for the exam.

faqs.question: What is the ideal time to start GATE 2026 preparation?
faqs.answer: There is no ideal time to start the GATE preparation. Start early (from the first year itself). It is mainly because your bachelor's topics and chapters have the most weightage in the GATE question paper. The topics that are taught in your third year are the backbone. If you are clear with the fundamentals and concepts (taught in classes), then you do not require extra time to prepare for GATE. Just revise and practice questions. That's enough. So, start preparing for GATE right from the first year. Your brain is fresh with the concepts and formulas, thus making it easy to solve the questions and prepare for the exam.

value: During this phase, candidates must take notes on their subject-specific syllabus and pattern and try to understand the complete syllabus-wise weightage and GATE 2026 exam pattern .

Aspirants must note that there is no ideal GATE preparation strategy . Here we have shared a generic preparation plan that students can implement to get the most benefit.
Understand the GATE exam pattern and syllabus

Candidates appearing for the Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering must understand their subject GATE exam pattern and marking scheme along with the syllabus. The question paper consists of the following types of questions -
Candidates must prepare according to their GATE branch paper .
Choose GATE study resources wisely

Aspirants must choose GATE preparation materials wisely. An ideal study material for the exam includes your textbook, one reference, mock test papers, followed with lecture notes. With these, students can categorise and plan their preparation smartly.

value: Start with textbooks, practice one chapter, go through notes
Solve chapter-wise full length mock test paper
Revise and solve question papers to evaluate your performance

blocks.value: There is no ideal time to start the GATE preparation. Start early (from the first year itself). It is mainly because your bachelor's topics and chapters have the most weightage in the GATE question paper. The topics that are taught in your third year are the backbone. If you are clear with the fundamentals and concepts (taught in classes), then you do not require extra time to prepare for GATE. Just revise and practice questions. That's enough.
So, start preparing for GATE right from the first year. Your brain is fresh with the concepts and formulas, thus making it easy to solve the questions and prepare for the exam.

Reserve at least two to three months for GATE revision. Grab your notes, formula handbooks, and shortcut tricks sheet and revise daily. Avoid starting anything new. Practice question papers and mock tests daily to build efficiency and accuracy to attempt the questions, and you are good to go.

Self-assessment is important when preparing for GATE because it helps you to understand GATE question paper format, where you are lagging in solving questions, etc. It is advised to revise and analyse after solving each paper.

value: Do not neglect previous year's question papers. Many times, the questions have been repeated. Also, with the help of the old question papers, students can get an idea about the difficulty level.
Do not rely only on coaching and online videos. Try to study notes and textbooks as well.
Do not ignore General Aptitude and Engineering Mathematics questions, as they can fetch you good marks in GATE

The Indian Institute of Technology, Guwahati, has started GATE 2026 admissions. Registrations are over. The GATE 2026 correction window is NOW OPEN till November 10. Candidates can edit their application form at the GOAPS portal. The GATE 2026 examination will take place on February 7, 8, 14, and 15.

Based on the latest news and events related to changes in the syllabus, exam pattern, dates, or any other related topics will be updated in this section of GATE 2026 latest news and updates on this page below. Candidates are suggested to visit our page for the latest update and news on GATE 2026.
